heroText: Vienna is a grand but easy city of imperial palaces, coffeehouses and efficient trams. Start with St. Stephen's Cathedral in the Innere Stadt, spend half a day at Schonbrunn Palace, then pair the Hofburg with MuseumsQuartier or Belvedere. Vienna International Airport links smoothly to the centre, making the city simple for rail and flight arrivals.

areas.name: Innere Stadt
areas.text: The first district keeps St. Stephen's Cathedral, the Hofburg and major museums within short walks, but hotel prices run high.

areas.name: Leopoldstadt
areas.text: Leopoldstadt sits across the Danube Canal with Prater access, good transit and calmer prices than the old centre.

areas.name: Wieden
areas.text: Wieden is close to Belvedere, the main station and cafes, useful for rail arrivals and longer city stays.

areas.name: Neubau
areas.text: Neubau borders MuseumsQuartier with independent shops, restaurants and nightlife west of the Ringstrasse.

airports.name: Vienna International Airport (VIE)
airports.text: Vienna International Airport is southeast of the city; rail links and airport buses make transfers straightforward for most central stays.

airportTransfer.value: 16-30 min by airport rail or 25-40 min by taxi to central Vienna
airportTransfer.distance: about 18 km southeast of the centre

stayOverview: Stay in the Innere Stadt for classic sightseeing, Leopoldstadt for better value and Prater access, Wieden for the main station and Belvedere, or Neubau for MuseumsQuartier, restaurants and a less formal evening base.
hotelIntro: Vienna's U-Bahn and tram network make hotel choice forgiving. Pay more for the Innere Stadt, look to Leopoldstadt for family value, Wieden for rail convenience, and Neubau for culture-led city breaks.
rentalCars: Avoid renting a car in Vienna; public transport is excellent and parking is a nuisance unless leaving for countryside drives.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose the Innere Stadt for a first short visit, or Neubau if restaurants and MuseumsQuartier matter more.

travelTips.title: Airport train
travelTips.text: Check the route from Vienna International Airport (VIE) before choosing between a central hotel and an airport-area first night in Vienna.

travelTips.title: Museum timing
travelTips.text: Keep one indoor culture stop in the Vienna plan so rain, heat or short winter daylight do not break the day.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Bratislava is close enough for a rail or boat day trip if Vienna is your longer base.

highlights.title: Schonbrunn Palace
highlights.text: Schonbrunn Palace is the former Habsburg summer residence, with state rooms, gardens and a long park axis west of the centre.
highlights.name: Schonbrunn Palace

highlights.title: St. Stephen's Cathedral
highlights.text: St. Stephen's Cathedral is one of Vienna's religious landmarks; check visiting hours and dress expectations before building the route around it.
highlights.name: St. Stephen's Cathedral

highlights.title: Hofburg
highlights.text: The Hofburg anchors imperial Vienna with museums, courtyards, the Spanish Riding School and state buildings inside the Ringstrasse.
highlights.name: Hofburg

history.label: 19th century
history.text: During the 19th century as the capital of the Austrian Empire and later Austria-Hungary, it temporarily became one of Europe's biggest cities.
In 1918, after World War I, Vienna became the capital of the Republic of German-Austria, and then in 1919 of the First Republic of Austria.

nearby.name: Wachau Valley
nearby.label: Wine
nearby.text: Terraced Grüner Veltliner vineyards along the Danube, with Dürnstein's blue abbey tower above them.

nearby.name: Bratislava
nearby.label: Town
nearby.text: A second capital within commuting distance: castle hill, a compact old town and far lower prices.

nearby.text: Sulphur baths the Habsburgs used, in a Biedermeier spa town with a rose garden and casino.
